input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Courtyard Gambit" is a 2019 short story by Austrian writer Lena Hofbauer.
- It follows Viktor and Mrs. Brenner, two elderly residents of a Vienna boarding house.
- At first, the two neighbors exchange only curt nods and complaints about noise.
- They begin a daily chess match, calling out moves across the shared courtyard from their windows.
- By the story's end, Mrs. Brenner leaves a pot of soup outside Viktor's door when he falls ill.
- Hofbauer has said she wanted to show how routine can quietly build intimacy.
input.question: The student wants to describe how the relationship between the story's two main characters changes over time. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Viktor and Mrs. Brenner, who initially share only curt nods and noise complaints, grow so close through their daily courtyard chess match that she brings him soup when he falls ill.
Viktor and Mrs. Brenner, two elderly residents of a Vienna boarding house, play a daily chess match by calling out moves across the shared courtyard from their windows.
Viktor and Mrs. Brenner, the central figures of Lena Hofbauer's 2019 story, reflect the author's stated aim of showing how routine can quietly build intimacy.
Viktor and Mrs. Brenner, neighbors in a Vienna boarding house, begin the story exchanging only curt nods and complaints about the noise in the building.
input.explanation: 목표는 두 인물의 관계가 시간에 따라 어떻게 변하는지 설명하는 것이므로, 처음 상태와 나중 상태를 함께 보여 줘야 합니다. A는 처음의 냉담함(짧은 목례와 소음 불평)과 마지막의 애정(아플 때 수프를 가져다줌)을 체스 경기라는 계기로 연결하므로 정답입니다. B는 날마다 두는 체스라는 일과만 설명할 뿐 관계의 처음과 끝을 보여 주지 않습니다. C는 작가의 의도를 전할 뿐, 인물들의 관계가 실제로 어떻게 변하는지는 보여 주지 않습니다. D는 처음의 냉담한 관계만 제시하고 변화의 결과가 빠져 있습니다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to show how the two characters' relationship changes over time, so the sentence needs both the starting point and the ending point. A does this: it gives their early coldness (curt nods and noise complaints) and their later affection (she brings him soup when he's sick), and it links the two through the chess match. B only describes the daily chess routine and never shows how the relationship started or ended up. C reports what the author meant to do, but it doesn't show the relationship actually changing. D gives only the cold beginning and leaves out the result of the change.
input.design: 세 오답이 각각 변화의 한 부분만 정확히 담고 있습니다(B는 계기, C는 작가의 주제, D는 처음 상태). 그래서 처음과 끝 상태를 모두 담았는지 확인해야만 정답을 고를 수 있습니다. 질문에는 'soup'이나 'coldness' 같은 정답 문구를 쓰지 않았습니다.

content.text: Notes about a fictional story; the goal is to emphasize that only Morag noticed the janitor's secret work, without naming it as "only noticed".

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Keeper of the Hours" is a short story by a fictional Scottish author, Eilidh Rankin.
- It is set at a two-room primary school on a remote Hebridean island.
- Morag, the story's nine-year-old protagonist, distrusts adults who claim to know things she cannot check for herself.
- The school's clock, installed more than a century earlier, keeps perfect time even though no repairer has visited the island in decades.
- Mr. Galbraith, the new janitor, quietly replaces the clock's worn gears with parts he carves from driftwood.
- Of all the pupils and teachers, Morag alone discovers what Mr. Galbraith is doing.
input.question: The student wants to show how the protagonist's personality relates to her role in the story's central discovery. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Eilidh Rankin's "The Keeper of the Hours," a century-old school clock on a remote Hebridean island keeps perfect time, even though no repairer has visited in decades.
In Eilidh Rankin's "The Keeper of the Hours," Morag, a nine-year-old who distrusts adults, attends a two-room primary school on a remote Hebridean island.
In Eilidh Rankin's "The Keeper of the Hours," the new janitor, Mr. Galbraith, secretly keeps the school's century-old clock running by carving replacement gears from driftwood.

In Eilidh Rankin's "The Keeper of the Hours," Morag, a nine-year-old unwilling to accept what she cannot verify herself, is the only person at her school to uncover the janitor's secret repairs to its clock.
input.explanation: 목표는 주인공의 성격과 이야기의 핵심 발견에서 그녀가 맡는 역할을 연결하는 것이다. D는 스스로 확인할 수 없는 것을 믿지 않는 Morag의 성격과, 그녀만이 관리인의 비밀 수리를 알아낸다는 사실을 함께 제시하므로 정답이다. B는 Morag의 성격을 언급하지만 발견에 대한 내용이 없고, 배경 설명에 그친다. C는 발견의 내용(관리인의 수리)은 담고 있지만 Morag와 그녀의 성격이 빠져 있다. A는 시계의 수수께끼만 소개할 뿐 주인공을 전혀 다루지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The goal asks you to link the protagonist's personality to her part in the story's central discovery. D does this: it describes Morag's refusal to accept what she can't verify and states that she alone uncovers the janitor's secret repairs. B mentions Morag's distrust, but it only gives the setting and says nothing about the discovery. C describes what the janitor is secretly doing, but it leaves out Morag and her personality entirely. A presents only the mystery of the clock and never mentions the protagonist.
input.design: Choices B and C each cover half of the goal (personality or discovery). D paraphrases the notes ("unwilling to accept what she cannot verify," "uncover") so the answer can't be found by matching words from the question.

content.text: Passage design: Dimitri and Yiannis have opened their kiosks together for thirty years. Concession then reversal: the ritual continues on the surface, but underneath they have drifted apart. The answer is "Still," (D). "However," was rejected as a distractor because it means almost the same thing, so the distractors use other relations.

input.passage: For thirty summers, Dimitri and Yiannis had raised the shutters of their neighboring kiosks on the Piraeus ferry dock at the same moment, each calling the first ferry's name to the other as if announcing a guest. This season, too, the shutters rose in unison, and the names were called on time. ______ Dimitri noticed that Yiannis no longer waited for his reply before turning to count the newspapers, and Dimitri himself had begun calling the names more out of habit than delight.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
In other words,
Similarly,
Still,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 올해도 의식이 겉으로는 그대로 이어졌다고 인정하고, 뒤 문장은 그 의식이 속으로는 비어 버렸다는 반대 사실을 보여 준다. 따라서 양보 후 반전을 나타내는 D가 정답이다. A는 뒤 문장을 앞 문장의 결과로 만들지만, 의식이 제때 이어진 것이 무관심의 원인은 아니다. B는 같은 내용을 바꿔 말하는 관계인데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 반대되는 내용을 담고 있다. C는 둘 다 의식에 관한 이야기여서 비슷해 보이지만, 지속과 공허는 서로 대비되는 내용이다.
input.explanation_en: The first sentence admits that the ritual looked the same as always this season. The next sentence shows that underneath, it had become empty. That is a concession followed by a reversal, so D is correct. A would make the friends' indifference a result of the ritual happening on time, but the ritual didn't cause it. B signals a restatement, yet the second sentence says the opposite of the first. C may look right because both sentences are about the ritual, but going through the motions and losing interest are contrasting ideas, not similar ones.
input.design: There is no word in the passage that hints at a contrast, such as "but" or "although." The reversal shows only in the content: the ritual looks the same on the outside but has gone hollow. Because every sentence is about the ritual, distractors that signal similarity, restatement, or result are tempting.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- "The Weight of Harvest" is a 2019 short story by Canadian writer Mara Lindqvist.
- Its protagonist, Callum, operates a grain elevator in rural Saskatchewan.
- At his sister Ingrid's wedding, Ingrid treasures a hand-carved wooden clock, believing Callum made it for her.
- Callum later learns the clock was actually carved by their late father as a gift for a neighbor's daughter.
- The story ends before Callum decides whether to tell Ingrid where the clock came from.
- Critics have praised Lindqvist's spare descriptions of prairie landscapes.
input.question: The student wants to present the central dilemma the protagonist faces in the story. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In Mara Lindqvist's "The Weight of Harvest," Callum must choose whether to tell Ingrid that the clock she cherishes, which she thinks he made, was actually carved by their father for someone else.
In Mara Lindqvist's "The Weight of Harvest," Callum, a grain-elevator operator in Saskatchewan, attends the wedding of his sister, Ingrid, who treasures a hand-carved wooden clock.
In Mara Lindqvist's "The Weight of Harvest," Callum learns that a wooden clock was carved by his late father as a gift for a neighbor's daughter.
In Mara Lindqvist's "The Weight of Harvest," Callum works at a grain elevator amid prairie landscapes that critics say are described in spare, praised prose.
input.explanation: 주인공의 핵심 딜레마를 제시하려면 '잉그리드가 시계를 캘럼이 만든 것으로 믿는다'는 정보와 '실제로는 아버지가 다른 사람을 위해 만들었다'는 정보, 그리고 진실을 말할지 결정해야 한다는 상황을 결합해야 한다. A는 이 세 요소를 모두 연결하므로 정답이다. B는 결혼식과 시계를 언급하지만 진실이 무엇인지, 무엇을 선택해야 하는지는 빠져 있다. C는 시계의 진짜 출처는 밝히지만 잉그리드의 오해와 캘럼이 내려야 할 결정이 없어 딜레마가 드러나지 않는다. D는 배경과 비평가의 평가에 집중해 목표와 무관하다.
input.explanation_en: To present the protagonist's central dilemma, you need to combine two facts: Ingrid believes Callum made the clock, but their father actually carved it for someone else. You also need the choice Callum faces about telling her the truth. Choice A connects all of these, so it is correct. Choice B mentions the wedding and the clock but leaves out the truth and the decision. Choice C gives the clock's real origin but leaves out Ingrid's mistaken belief and Callum's choice, so no dilemma comes through. Choice D focuses on the setting and the critics' praise, which has nothing to do with the goal.
input.design: B와 C는 각각 딜레마의 절반(오해 / 진실)만 담아, 두 메모를 연결해야만 정답 A를 고를 수 있게 했다. 질문은 '딜레마'라고만 표현해 선택지 A의 핵심어(choose, tell)를 그대로 쓰지 않았다.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Last Lesson at Ushguli (2019) is a novel by Nino Kavtaradze.
- It is set in a Svaneti village in the Georgian highlands during the 1970s.
- Its main character, Giorgi, is a schoolteacher who will retire at the end of the term.
- A district inspector from the Soviet education office requires every lesson to follow the state-issued textbook.
- In the novel's central scene, Giorgi leaves the textbook closed and teaches using only a river stone, a hawk feather, and a sprig of wild thyme.
- Each object is linked to a private memory that Giorgi never explains to his students.
input.question: The student wants to show how what Giorgi does in the novel's central scene differs from what officials expected of him. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Although Giorgi will retire at the end of the term, he still teaches a lesson in the novel's central scene, using a river stone, a hawk feather, and a sprig of wild thyme.
Although a Soviet district inspector requires every lesson to follow the state textbook, Giorgi keeps the book closed and teaches with only a river stone, a hawk feather, and a sprig of wild thyme.
Although each object Giorgi brings to class is linked to a private memory, he never explains those memories to the students in his Svaneti village school.
Although The Last Lesson at Ushguli was published in 2019, Nino Kavtaradze sets the novel, which centers on a teacher named Giorgi, in the Georgian highlands of the 1970s.
input.explanation: 목표는 장면 속 Giorgi의 행동이 당국의 기대와 어떻게 다른지 보여주는 것이므로, 장학관의 교과서 요구(기대)와 교과서를 덮고 자연물로 가르치는 행동을 함께 제시해야 한다. B는 이 두 메모를 결합해 대조를 분명히 드러낸다. A는 실제 행동은 언급하지만 대조 대상이 공식적 요구가 아니라 은퇴 시점이다. C는 개인적 기억과 침묵 사이의 대조일 뿐 당국의 기대가 빠져 있다. D는 출간 시기와 배경 시기를 대조할 뿐 Giorgi의 행동과 무관하다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to show how Giorgi's actions in the central scene differ from what officials expected, so you need both the official expectation (the inspector's textbook rule) and what Giorgi actually does (closes the book and teaches with natural objects). B puts these two notes together and makes the contrast clear. A describes the lesson, but it sets it against Giorgi's retirement, not against any official demand. C contrasts his private memories with his silence and never mentions what officials expected. D contrasts the publication date with the setting and says nothing about Giorgi's behavior.
input.design: To get this right, you have to link two separate notes: the inspector's rule and Giorgi's actual lesson. All four options use the same "Although…" sentence pattern, and A and C also mention the lesson objects, so you can only rule them out by checking what each sentence contrasts.

input.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Ruth Calloway's 2019 novel The Last Furrow is set on the Texas Panhandle in 1935.
- Its protagonist, Pearl Haskins, is a farmwife whose wheat crop has failed for three straight years.
- In one chapter, Pearl drives a mule wagon 31 miles through dust storms to the town of Dalhart.
- Her aim is to pick up a single packet of drought-resistant sorghum seed mailed to her by her late mother's sister.
- Calloway has said the chapter was inspired by her grandmother's diaries.
- Reviewers have praised the chapter's spare, unsentimental prose.
input.question: The student wants to explain the practical problem on Pearl's farm that motivates her journey in the chapter. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: In a chapter of The Last Furrow, Pearl Haskins drives a mule wagon 31 miles through dust storms to Dalhart, a journey Calloway based on her grandmother's diaries.
In a chapter of The Last Furrow, Pearl Haskins drives 31 miles to Dalhart through dust storms, an ordeal that reviewers say Calloway renders in spare, unsentimental prose.
In a chapter of The Last Furrow, Pearl Haskins, whose wheat has failed three years running, drives 31 miles through dust storms to Dalhart for a packet of drought-resistant sorghum seed.
In a chapter of The Last Furrow, Pearl Haskins drives 31 miles through dust storms to Dalhart to pick up a packet of seed mailed to her by her late mother's sister.
input.explanation: 목표는 Pearl의 여정을 촉발한 농장의 실질적 문제를 설명하는 것이다. C는 3년 연속 밀 농사 실패라는 문제와 가뭄에 강한 수수 씨앗이라는 해결책을 연결해 여정의 동기를 분명히 보여 준다. A는 여정과 작가의 영감 출처만 말할 뿐 농장 문제는 언급하지 않는다. B는 평론가의 문체 평가에 초점을 둔다. D는 씨앗을 가지러 간다는 목적은 밝히지만 작물 실패나 씨앗의 가뭄 내성을 빠뜨려 그것이 어떤 문제를 해결하는지 보여 주지 못한다.
input.explanation_en: Your goal is to explain the practical problem on the farm that drives Pearl's trip. C does this by linking two notes: her wheat has failed for three years, and the seed she is after is drought-resistant sorghum, so the trip is clearly a response to the failing crop. A covers the journey and where Calloway got the idea, but it never mentions any farm problem. B is about how reviewers judged the prose. D tells you she's going to get seed, but it leaves out the crop failure and the drought resistance, so you can't tell what problem the seed would solve.
input.design: 정답은 작물 실패와 가뭄 내성 씨앗이라는 두 메모를 결합해야 하며, D는 목적만 제시해 훑어 읽으면 정답처럼 보이도록 설계했다. 모든 선택지는 같은 문장 틀을 쓴다.

input.passage: On her first morning at the mountain bus station outside Oaxaca, Rosa assumed the elderly vendor's blankets were simply decorative, their zigzags and diamonds chosen for color alone. By the third day, after the woman had guided Rosa's hands through the first rows of a pattern on the small backstrap loom, Rosa understood that each zigzag marked a river crossing and each diamond a village her ancestors had left behind. ______ the bus she had been so impatient to board now seemed less like a rescue than an interruption.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Nevertheless,
For example,
As a result,
In other words,
input.design: 빈칸 뒤 문장은 앞 문장의 깨달음이 가져온 감정 변화(결과)이며, 어휘 단서 없이 인과 방향을 판단해야 한다. 오답 Nevertheless는 표면적 태도 반전에, In other words는 '재진술'이라는 착각에 끌리도록 설계했다.
input.explanation: 앞 문장에서 Rosa는 무늬마다 가족의 이야기가 담겨 있다는 것을 깨닫고, 뒤 문장에서는 그 깨달음 때문에 버스가 더 이상 반갑지 않게 느껴진다. 따라서 원인과 결과를 잇는 C가 정답이다. A는 Rosa의 태도가 바뀌었다는 점 때문에 대조처럼 보이지만, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장의 깨달음과 충돌하는 것이 아니라 그 깨달음에서 자연스럽게 나온 결과이다. B는 뒤 문장이 무늬의 의미를 보여 주는 구체적 사례가 아니므로 맞지 않는다. D는 버스에 대한 느낌이 무늬의 의미를 다시 말한 것이 아니라 새로운 정보이므로 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: In the earlier sentence, Rosa realizes that each pattern holds part of her family's story. The final sentence then shows what that realization does to her: the bus no longer feels welcome. Since the second sentence is a consequence of the first, C is correct. A might be tempting because Rosa's attitude shifts, but the final sentence doesn't contradict her realization; it follows naturally from it. B doesn't work because how she feels about the bus isn't an example of what the patterns mean, and D doesn't work because that feeling is new information, not a restatement of the earlier point.

content.text:
Need passage: literary fiction, transition without lexical cue. Design: concession then reversal? e.g., "Each morning Feldman left a single rose... Richter countered with a sonnet... By the third week the landlady had started to find the gifts tiresome. ______, neither man showed signs of stopping." Answer "Nevertheless,"? That's cued by "tiresome"... fine for medium. Wrong: "Consequently," (partially: effects), "In other words," "For example,". Make it subtler: The gestures were never really for the landlady... Let me write.

Passage: "In the winter of 1947, Dr. Feldman and Herr Richter waged a quiet war for the favor of Frau Hölzl, who ran the boarding house on Gumpendorfer Strasse. Feldman polished her doorknob each evening; Richter responded by reciting Rilke to her geraniums. Frau Hölzl, for her part, found both men exhausting and said so plainly at breakfast. ______, the gestures continued, each more elaborate than the last, as if the two men needed the contest more than they needed to win it."
Answer A "Even so,". Others: "As a result," (plausible if read gestures continuing as a reaction), "Similarly,", "In particular,".

input.passage: In the winter of 1947, Dr. Feldman and Herr Richter waged a quiet war for the favor of Frau Hölzl, who ran the boarding house on Gumpendorfer Strasse. Feldman polished the brass doorknob of her sitting room each evening; Richter answered by reciting Rilke to her potted geraniums. Frau Hölzl, for her part, found both men exhausting and told them so plainly over breakfast. ______ the gestures continued, each more elaborate than the last, as though the two men needed the contest far more than they needed to win it.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Even so,
As a result,
Similarly,
In particular,
input.explanation: Frau Hölzl가 두 남자에게 지쳤다고 분명히 말했으므로 구애 행동은 멈추는 게 자연스럽다. 그런데도 행동이 오히려 더 정교해지며 계속되었으므로, 예상과 어긋나는 결과를 이어 주는 A가 정답이다. B는 행동이 이어진 것을 그녀의 거절이 낳은 결과로 만들어 버리는데, 마지막 구절이 경쟁 자체에 대한 두 남자의 욕구를 이유로 들기 때문에 인과 방향이 맞지 않는다. C는 앞 문장과 비슷한 내용을 덧붙일 때 쓰는 말인데, 이 문장은 거절과 비슷한 내용이 아니라 그에 반하는 내용이다. D는 앞 내용의 구체적인 사례를 들 때 쓰는 말이지만, 행동이 계속되었다는 것은 그녀의 불평을 구체화한 예가 아니다.
input.explanation_en: Frau Hölzl plainly told both men they exhausted her, so you would expect the gestures to stop. Instead, they kept going and got more elaborate, so you need a transition that marks a result running against expectation, which is choice A. Choice B makes the continued gestures a consequence of her rebuke, but the final clause says they continued because the men needed the contest itself, so the cause-and-effect direction is wrong. Choice C signals an added point like the one before, but this sentence goes against her rebuke rather than echoing it. Choice D introduces a specific example, but the gestures continuing is not an example of her complaint.
input.design: 빈칸 앞의 명시적 거절 후, 기대를 깨는 지속이 오는 양보-반전 구조다. As a result는 행동이 '그녀의 반응 이후'에 이어진다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 마지막 구절이 행동의 진짜 원인을 따로 제시하므로 배제된다.

content.text:
Need a literary passage with a transition logic, e.g., concession then reversal. Design: Thanh could hammer out dents; she knows a coppersmith would; yet she leaves them. Let's write.

Passage: "Each morning before the alley stirs, Thanh rubs ash into the aluminum pot her grandmother carried out of Nam Định in 1954. A metalworker on Hàng Đồng Street once offered to beat the pot smooth for a few thousand đồng, and Thanh admits the dents make it wobble on her charcoal stove. ______ she polishes only around them, tracing with her thumb the deep crease left when her father dropped the pot fleeing the bombing of 1972 and the shallow one from her own crossing to the city."

Answer: Still, (concession then reversal). Distractors: Accordingly, (cause—partial since wobble suggests fixing, but she doesn't), For instance, , Likewise, . Options: A Accordingly, B Still, C For example, D Similarly,. Need non-Korean in passage; diacritics fine.

input.passage: Each morning before the alley wakes, Thanh rubs wood ash into the aluminum pot her grandmother carried south out of Nam Dinh in 1954. A metalworker on Hang Dong Street once offered to hammer the pot smooth for almost nothing, and Thanh freely admits that its dents make it rock unsteadily on her charcoal stove. ______ she scrubs only around them, tracing with her thumb the deep crease left when her father dropped the pot while fleeing the bombing of 1972 and the shallow one from her own bus ride to the city.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Accordingly,
Still,
For example,
Similarly,
input.explanation: 앞 문장은 수리 제안이 있었고 찌그러짐 때문에 냄비가 흔들린다는 점, 즉 냄비를 펴야 할 이유를 Thanh가 인정한다는 내용이다. 그런데 뒤 문장에서 그녀는 찌그러진 곳을 그대로 두고 그 주변만 닦는다. 이처럼 양보한 뒤 반전되는 관계이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 결과를 나타내는데, 앞 내용대로라면 냄비를 고쳐야 자연스러우므로 방향이 반대다. C는 뒤 문장이 앞 내용의 예시가 아니므로 맞지 않고, D는 두 행동이 서로 비슷하지 않고 대조되므로 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The previous sentence gives reasons to fix the pot: someone offered to repair it cheaply, and Thanh admits the dents make it rock on the stove. The next sentence shows her doing the opposite. She keeps the dents and cleans only around them. That is a concession followed by a reversal, so B is correct. A signals a result, but the logical result of those reasons would be fixing the pot, not keeping the dents. C doesn't work because the sentence isn't an example of what came before, and D doesn't work because her action contrasts with those reasons rather than resembling them.
input.design: Neither sentence contains a contrast word. Students have to see that admitting the reasons for repair and then keeping the dents creates a concession-then-reversal relationship. A tempts students who read only the second sentence as a reasonable consequence of caring for the pot.

input.passage: Amira turned the old water pouch over on her workbench in the tannery. At first glance it looked like the work of a single craftsman: the outer goat hide was evenly dyed, and its seams were closed with the same coarse waxed thread her master used on every pouch he sold in the Fez market. ______ when she slit the cracked seam to repair it, she found a lining of camel leather beneath the goat hide, and beneath that a third layer stitched with a knot she had seen only in her grandmother's stories of the caravans that once crossed the Sahara to Timbuktu.
input.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: In fact,
Still,
Similarly,
As a result,
input.explanation: 첫 문장은 겉보기에 파우치가 한 장인의 작품처럼 보인다는 인상을 제시하고, 다음 문장은 솔기를 열자 여러 시대·여러 손의 층이 드러났다는, 그 인상을 뒤집는 내용이다. 따라서 겉모습을 인정한 뒤 반전시키는 B가 가장 논리적이다. A는 앞 문장의 주장을 강화할 때 쓰므로, 단일 장인이라는 인상과 충돌하는 발견에는 맞지 않는다. C는 두 대상의 유사점을 잇는데, 층마다 다르다는 점은 유사성이 아니라 대조다. D는 겉모습이 균일하다는 사실이 숨은 층을 발견하게 한 원인인 것처럼 만들지만, 그런 인과 관계는 없다.
input.explanation_en: The first sentence gives the impression that the pouch was made by a single craftsman, and the next sentence reveals hidden layers from different makers and eras, which overturns that impression. So B fits best, because it accepts how the pouch first looked and then turns against it. A is used to strengthen the point before it, but the hidden layers go against the single-maker impression instead of supporting it. C connects things that are alike, but the layers stand in contrast to the pouch's uniform surface. D would mean the even dye and matching seams caused Amira to find the hidden layers, and the text shows no such cause-and-effect link.
input.design: There's no "but"-type word in the passage to give the answer away. Students have to see that the first sentence sets up a "single maker" impression and the second overturns it. Some wrong choices are tempting: A because "in fact" can sound like a reveal, C because both sentences describe stitching, and D because Amira's discovery follows her inspection of the pouch.
